correctness.rationale: For each pair of adjacent candidate final sampling times, a threshold-based adjacent transposition is an exchangeability-preserving involution. It preserves the ordered full-record heights and the full unordered multiset, and transfers the retained-subsequence final record indicator pointwise. The complete all-size proof handles ties. For iid atomless inputs independent insertion ranks and two exact events yield covariance 1/(2k(k+1)). A standalone exhaustive exact checker verified 49,508 words and 21,170,019 identities but finite tests are not relied upon as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The entire joint law of full-sequence record values and the record count of a partially observed subsequence cannot identify the last observation time once earlier sampling positions are fixed, uniformly over all finite exchangeable laws including ties and dependence. This is a natural design non-identifiability for record statistics, not a routine marginal record-law calculation; the exact two-position covariance isolates the first-observation location as the sharp source of remaining dependence.
